Rising Costs Threaten Notebook Demand in 2027, Raising Risks of Shipment Declines and Price Increases, Says TrendForce

8 October 2026

TrendForce's latest notebook industry research reveals that the primary risk facing the market in 2027 is expected to shift from supply constraints to the impact of rising costs on demand. Global notebook shipments are currently projected to decline by a low-single-digit percentage in 2027.

Six Leading Suppliers Bet on VCSEL NPO; VCSEL Demand Projected to Reach 650 Million Units by 2031, Says TrendForce

8 October 2026

TrendForce’s latest report, “2027 Infrared Sensing and Optical Communication Market Trend”, shows that rapidly growing demand for data transmission in expanding data center networks is increasing interest in VCSEL-based near-packaged optics (NPO). This technology is favored for its low power usage, easier maintenance, and a mature supply chain. Major companies like Lumentum, Furukawa Electric, Coherent, Broadcom, ams OSRAM, and HiSilicon are investing heavily in R&D.

AI Server Demand Sustains Memory Contract Price Increases in 4Q26, While Consumer-Side Pressure Persists, Says TrendForce

30 September 2026

TrendForce’s latest memory industry research reveals that DRAM suppliers continue to prioritize advanced-process capacity for high-performance server products in 4Q26, keeping the overall market undersupplied. However, the pace of contract price increases is expected to moderate, with conventional DRAM prices projected to rise 10–15% QoQ.

HBM Supply Constraints Persist, 2027 Price Outlook Revised Upward with Blended ASP Forecast to Rise 121% YoY, Says TrendForce

29 September 2026

TrendForce’s latest research reveals that continued expansion in AI server demand is keeping HBM and conventional DRAM in competition for limited advanced-process and wafer capacity. Meanwhile, yields and output for next-generation products will take time to ramp, keeping memory supply tight through 2027.

Japanese and Korean MLCC Makers Cut Consumer Supply to Focus on AI, Chinese Suppliers Enter Global Brand Qualification, Says TrendForce

24 September 2026

According to TrendForce, the MLCC industry is experiencing a structural shift as AI demand continues to displace traditional markets. Leading Japanese and Korean suppliers are increasingly reducing their supply of consumer-oriented MLCCs and reallocating capacity to AI-related applications. This change is opening doors for Chinese suppliers, many of whom are now undergoing MLCC qualification with global brands such as Dell, HP, ASUS, and Acer.
